name: Osteopathia Striata with Pigmentary Dermopathy and White Forelock Syndrome
aliases: Osteopathia Striata with Pigmentary Dermopathy and Leukotrichia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Osteopathia Striata-Pigmentary Dermopathy-White Forelock Syndrome

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of linear striations in the metaphyses and diaphyses of long bones
Presence of characteristic reticulated or streaked hyperpigmented skin lesions
Congenital white forelock or leukotrichia of the scalp hair
Mild facial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: osteopathia striata on imaging, pigmentary dermopathy, and white forelock
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic findings; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormality of pelvic girdle bone morphology

imaging: Radiographs showing linear striations in metaphyses and diaphyses of long bones
Skeletal survey to identify associated anomalies
genetic: Mutations in AMER1 (WTX) gene associated with X-linked dominant inheritance
Genetic testing may confirm diagnosis but not always definitive
other: Clinical examination revealing white forelock and pigmentary skin changes
Family history consistent with inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cranial sclerosis and facial dysmorphism without pigmentary dermopathy
Progressive skin changes with vesicular and verrucous stages

references: OMIM Entry #300373 - Osteopathia Striata with Pigmentary Dermopathy and White Forelock Syndrome
Orphanet Report on Osteopathia Striata with Pigmentary Dermopathy and White Forelock Syndrome, ORPHA:2779
